options-flow-feed-lab.lean=balanced; callFraction=0.4023; callPremium=1433.7M; putPremium=2130.2M; contracts=1729; tickers=12
items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium and the VIX band to judge whether an index holding near its high is being carried by a set of leaders that has narrowed but not collapsed.
items.note: A mild narrow-leadership divergence carries into the after-hours window. The SPY benchmark closed at 767.45, only 1.34% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.39%, 200-day +9.07%, 126-day momentum +12.99%), yet just 55.23% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 4.77-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold. Premium flow is not confirming the strength: it reads balanced but tilts defensive, with calls only 40.2% of premium (about $1.43B of call premium against $2.13B of puts) across 12 tickers and 1729 flagged contracts. VIX 15.84 keeps this in a calm, pressure-not-panic band, while swing structure now reads bull-stacked with an active, qualified double-top pattern over 518 bars. A headline index pinned near its high on roughly 55% breadth, with hedging premium leading and a double top forming overhead, is a milder version of the thinning-leadership pattern: participation is broader than a deep divergence but still under the healthy line. What to watch is whether breadth re-broadens back above the 60% threshold or the tape converges down toward the narrower leaders.
items.title: SPY holds about 1.3% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked regime while daily breadth stalls just below 60% and premium flow leans defensive

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative; signedNetGEX=-3.25B; flip=773.37; callWall=774; putWall=767; expectedMove=2.49; spot=767.41; atmIV=0.0876

items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current spot, size the expected-move band, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the intraday session type and VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on the lower edge of the gamma structure this window. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$3.25B, and SPY spot 767.41 has slipped well below the 773.37 flip to sit right on the 767 put wall, with the 774 call wall overhead. The front expected move is a tight plus or minus 2.49, so the 767-to-774 wall corridor is narrow and both walls bracket spot. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure at a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape agrees at the level: among the most unusual prints is a same-day SPY 768 put at $59.4M on 222.4x open interest, printed right at the put wall, alongside a 1-day AMD 480 call and an MSFT 485 call. The live auction is a range day under mixed control with VWAP 768.08 just above spot after a 0.52% gap-down open. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure with a patient, same-session-fade playbook: while 767 holds and VIX 15.84 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 767 put wall in short-gamma is what would tip the balance toward downside acceleration rather than a fade.
items.title: SPY spot rests at the 767 put wall below the 773.37 negative-gamma flip as the same-day tape sells a $59M SPY 768 put
